sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the entire record.

This criminal appeal under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been preferred by the appellant with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 17.06.2022 passed by the Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Allahabad.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that he is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.
It is also submitted that the victim was major and married lady and was in relation with the present appellant and she was living with him as wife.

When he went to Mumbai she came at the house of appellant and threatened the members of his family to give money when refused, present F.I.R. was lodged against the appellant and other members of his family for commission of rape and assault with her.
It is also submitted that during medical examination no any injury was found on the person of the victim to suggest that rape was committed with her by the appellant.
In the F.I.R. incident is said to have taken place on two days i.e. 24.08.2021 and 28.08.2021.
The injury said to be found on the person of the victim does not support the allegation of rape.
It is also submitted that as per jail record the victim went to meet appellant in jail several times and shown herself as wife.
The appellant is being harassed by the victim for making pressure on him to live with her.
The trial court while passing the impugned order did not take into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.
The appellant is languishing in jail since 09.05.2022 having no any criminal antecedent.
Learned counsel for the appellant also referred to the amended provisions of SC/ST Act.
All these facts were not taken into consideration by the learned Special Judge while rejecting the bail which cannot be said to be lawful, therefore requested to set it aside and allow the appeal.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, the period of the appellant remained in jail, the jail record, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
The learned court erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned order suffers from infirmity and illegality and the same is liable to be set-aside and the appeal is to be allowed.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order rejecting the bail application of the appellant is set-aside.

Let the appellant Bablu alias Mohd. Suhail involved in Case Crime No. 518 of 2021 under Sections 452, 323, 328, 376-D and 506 I.P.C. and 3(2)Va SC/ST Act, Police Station Mau Aima, District Prayagraj be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.

2. The appellant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

5. The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
